Estimate a partial correlation network

Source: R/correlation.R
pcor_network.Rd

pcor_network() estimates a partial correlation network, in which each pair of variables is joined by their correlation after controlling for all other variables in the network. An edge is therefore an association that the remaining variables do not account for, and for normally distributed data a partial correlation of zero means that the two variables are conditionally independent.

This is the unregularized Gaussian graphical model, in which every partial correlation is estimated and none is set to zero by the model itself. The partial correlations are computed from the inverse of the correlation matrix of raw data or of a supplied correlation matrix. alpha keeps only partial correlations that differ significantly from zero, with an optional multiple-comparison adjustment (adjust), and threshold removes weak ones.

pcor_network() returns the partial correlations as a network; the network involves no optimization and has no certificate.

With many variables relative to the sample size, partial correlations are estimated with large error, and with fewer observations than variables they are not identified. ebic_glasso() and ggm_modselect() then estimate a sparse network instead; cor_network() gives the marginal correlations. The network is the "pcor" estimator of bootnet.

Usage

pcor_network(
  data = NULL,
  cor_matrix = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  cor_method = c("pearson", "spearman", "kendall", "auto"),
  threshold = 0,
  alpha = NULL,
  adjust = "none",
  na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise"),
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A numeric data frame or matrix with one row per observation. Not needed when cor_matrix is given. Ordered factors enter as their level codes; other non-numeric columns are dropped with a message, and constant or all-missing columns with a warning.

cor_matrix

A correlation matrix to use instead of data; a covariance matrix is rescaled to a correlation matrix. With alpha, n is then required.

n

Sample size of cor_matrix, needed only for the significance test: a single number >= 1, and a whole number >= 3 when alpha is set. Ignored when data is given.

cor_method

Correlation computed from data: "pearson" (default), "spearman", "kendall", or "auto" (polychoric and polyserial correlations for ordinal items; see cor_auto()).

threshold

Absolute edge weight below which an edge is set to zero: a single number >= 0. Default 0. A logical value (the threshold = TRUE rule of qgraph) is refused; use alpha for a significance rule.

alpha

Significance level in (0, 1): edges not significant at this level are set to zero. Default NULL, no test. A Kendall test needs raw data; partial Kendall correlations cannot be tested.

adjust

Multiple-comparison adjustment of the edge p-values, any method of stats::p.adjust(). Default "none".

na_method

Handling of missing values in data: "pairwise" (default) uses pairwise-complete correlations adjusted to the nearest positive-definite matrix; "listwise" drops incomplete rows. The two agree for complete data.

labels

Optional node labels, one unique label per node of the network.

Value

A fitted network of class psychnet (psychnet) whose edge weights are partial correlations. as.data.frame() returns one row per edge with columns from, to and weight; certificate() reports that the network has no certificate. The object also stores the precision matrix (precision), the correlation matrix (cor_matrix), the sample size (n_eff), the missing-data handling used (na_method), the observations per pair when estimated from data (n_pair) and, with alpha, the unadjusted p-values (p_values). Nodes keep the column order of the input.

Details

With \(\Theta\) the inverse correlation matrix, the partial correlation of variables \(i\) and \(j\) is \(-\Theta_{ij} / \sqrt{\Theta_{ii}\Theta_{jj}}\). The significance test is described in cor_network(); for \(p\) variables it has \(n - p\) degrees of freedom. It needs a single sample size, so with pairwise data whose pairs have different numbers of observations alpha is refused.

When the correlation matrix is singular, as with fewer observations than variables or with collinear or duplicate columns, the nearest positive-definite matrix is inverted so that a network is still returned, and a warning says that its edges are not interpretable.

Conditions

psychnet_singular (warning) when the correlation matrix is singular or nearly so; psychnet_degenerate_sample (error, also of class psychnet_bad_input) when the sample is too small for the test (\(n \le p\)); psychnet_bad_input when an argument is out of range, threshold is logical, alpha is combined with Kendall correlations or with unequal pairwise sample sizes, cor_matrix is not a finite, symmetric, positive semi-definite matrix with a positive diagonal, n is missing with cor_matrix and alpha, data has fewer than two usable variables, or labels do not match the nodes; psychnet_constant_variable (warning) when a constant or all-missing column is dropped.

See also

cor_network(); ebic_glasso() and ggm_modselect() for sparse networks; psychnet(), which routes method = "pcor" here; psychnet for the result.

Examples

x <- matrix(stats::rnorm(200 * 4), 200, 4)
pcor_network(x)
#> <psychnet> pcor network
#>   nodes: 4   edges: 6   (undirected)
pcor_network(x, alpha = 0.05, adjust = "holm")
#> <psychnet> pcor network
#>   nodes: 4   edges: 0   (undirected)
